title: Bug0 Releases QA Agent to Automate Regression Testing With Cached Playwright Replays
gist: Linearbytes' Bug0 QA Agent is a source-available Playwright library that uses an LLM agent for first-run UI exploration, caches single-action steps for fast replay, self-heals on UI changes, and verifies assertions via multi-model (Claude, Gemini, tie-breaker) vision consensus. It targets the latency, cost and flakiness of fully agentic testing; research shows autonomous testers agree with humans only ~60% of the time.

insights.claim: Bug0 QA Agent decouples initial agentic visual exploration from routine regression runs by compiling successful single-action steps into concrete browser operations cached in Redis and replayed through Playwright without new LLM inference.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Caching LLM-derived actions is a practical pattern to cut agent latency and token cost.
insights.quote: On following runs, the suite replays the cached action directly through Playwright, eschewing the latency cost of a new LLM inference.

insights.claim: When UI changes break a cached action, Bug0 invalidates the cache and re-invokes the multimodal agent rather than failing the run; multi-action steps are never cached and re-run through the agent every time.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Self-healing tests reduce maintenance cost but complex steps keep paying LLM costs.
insights.quote: caching applies only to single-action steps; complex, multi-action directives re-execute through the agent on every run.

insights.claim: Assertions are never cached: Claude and Gemini independently evaluate each assertion via vision models with a third model breaking ties, and video models catch transient UI defects like auto-dismissing toasts.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Multi-model consensus is emerging as a reliability pattern for LLM judgments.
insights.quote: Claude and Gemini independently evaluate every assertion, with a third model breaking ties.

themes.theme: Limits of legacy and AI-first testing

insights.claim: Legacy automated tests depend on implementation details like CSS classes and data-testid, causing rewrites when specs are unchanged, and suffer flakiness from asynchronous distributed systems.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Persistent test-maintenance pain is the market opening for AI testing tools.

insights.claim: AI-first testing adds several seconds of LLM latency per step, escalates token costs and adds non-determinism-driven flakiness, making it impractical for large regression suites, though it resists implementation changes well.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Pure agentic approaches are cost/latency-bound; hybrids win near-term.
insights.quote: LLMs can routinely add several seconds of latency per step, escalate API token costs, and introduce their own brand of flakyness

insights.claim: Chevrot et al. found their best autonomous testing agent agreed with professional human testers in only about 60% of runs, citing assertion verifiability and grounding as the main levers for improvement; the study used GPT-4o, Sonnet and Gemini in April 2025.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: Autonomous testing reliability was still far from human parity as of that study.

insights.claim: Bug0 QA Agent is released under the Functional Source License 1.1 with ALv2 future license, a source-available, non-open-source license imposing non-compete restrictions for two years, pioneered by Sentry to avoid free-riding.
insights.speaker: Bruno Couriol
insights.so_what: FSL adoption continues among dev-tool startups seeking to block cloud free-riders.
